decisions.statement: A caller reaches the pages through this module rather than through a store of its own.
The shapes sent and answered are the service's own types rather than copies.
A question names its page type as `pageTypeSlug`.
A write hands over values under `pages` rather than a path and a body.
The origin is read from the environment before anything else.
A browser reaches the service under its own origin.
A caller may put its own fetcher in place of the global fetcher.
A call that answers nothing is tried again.
A call the service refuses for its own reasons is not tried again.
A refusal the service states is carried into the reason given back.
A reason names how many attempts were spent and where those attempts went.
An answer whose shape is not the shape asked for is refused rather than read on.
A body that will not read as JSON is refused rather than answered as nothing.
A refusal over a body that will not read has the parser's message.
A refusal over a body that will not read names how many bytes came back.
A body that will not read as JSON is not tried again.
A page type's shape is asked for through this module.
A page's file is asked for through this module as a question is.
A file answered well is taken as bytes rather than read as JSON.
A file answered badly is read as JSON to find the reason.
A file the service refuses for its own reasons is not asked for again.
A shape answered as no page type is refused rather than read on.
Nothing here opens a page's file.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here knows the properties a page type declares.
The waiting between attempts outlasts the pages system service starting again.
A write may keep values outside the commit beside a path.
Nothing here appends to a page's file part, though the service answers appends.

definition: the pages asked for and written over HTTP by whoever is not the workstation
